title: Tiered Evaluation Orchestration and Label-Refresh Playbook
author: Priya Desai
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a tiered evaluation orchestration pattern and an automated label-refresh loop for long-tail prompt coverage, focused on mixed-mode deployments (hosted, dedicated, private). It prescribes how to prioritize evaluation resources, run quantization-aware regressions, and triage failures back into an automated labeling and resampling pipeline. The intent is to keep production quality stable while minimizing eval cost and human labeling overhead.

Why this matters:
- Production workloads are long-tailed: a small fraction of prompts account for most customer pain.
- Evaluations must balance fidelity (expensive, exact reproductions) with throughput (cheap, wide coverage).
- Quantization and model forks (e.g., quantized variants) introduce subtle failure modes that only surface with targeted prompt resampling.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: applied ML engineers, evaluation owners, QA engineers, model-serving SREs, and solutions engineers supporting Private deployments.
- Scope: continuous eval orchestration, prompt resample prioritization, label-refresh automation, quantization-aware gating and regression triage. Does not cover billing, customer communication templates, or security incident response (see related pages).

Components overview:
1) Eval Orchestrator (service: evald) — schedules and prioritizes evaluation jobs across three tiers: rapid-smoke, focused-slice, and fidelity-replay.
2) Resample Prioritizer (service: samplecraft) — scores prompt/document slices for human labeling or synthetic augmentation.
3) Label Refresh Pipeline (job: label-refresher) — batches human tasks and applies labels back to the eval corpus with provenance.
4) Regression Triage Assistant (tool: triage-assist) — links failing slices to potential root causes: prompt drift, quantization delta, KV-cache mismatch, or model-version idiosyncrasy.
5) Telemetry connector — maps production traces and error tags back to eval slices.

Tier definitions and when to use them:
- Tier 1: Rapid-smoke (low-cost, high-frequency)
  - Purpose: detect large regressions quickly after a build or config change.
  - Characteristics: synthetic seeds + small high-impact prompt sets, latency < 5 min, cost < 2% of full eval budget.
  - Use cases: pre-commit smoke, post-deploy quick sanity checks.

- Tier 2: Focused-slice (medium-cost, targeted)
  - Purpose: validate behavior on high-risk slices (business-critical customers, high-error cohorts, long-context sequences).
  - Characteristics: human-labeled reference answers, ensemble comparators, targeted metrics (semantic-f1, calibration, hallucination score).
  - Use cases: canary promotions, quantization candidate validation.

- Tier 3: Fidelity-replay (high-cost, low-frequency)
  - Purpose: reproduce exact production traces with live KV/state, full RNG seeds, and quantized/FP variants for root-cause analysis.
  - Characteristics: exact sequence lengths, real traffic mirrors, token-level diffs, full telemetry correlation.
  - Use cases: regression postmortems, model certification for Private deployments.

Prioritization policy (Resample Prioritizer):
- Input signals (scored, 0–100): production error rate delta, traffic weight, novelty score (NLP embedding distance to training set), last-labeled-at (recency penalty), and quantization-sensitivity score.
- Score formula (example): 0.4*error_delta + 0.25*traffic_weight + 0.2*novelty + 0.1*quant_sensitivity + 0.05*recency_boost.
- Buckets: High (>70), Medium (40–70), Low (<40).
- Actions: High -> immediate human labeling batch + Tier 2 eval; Medium -> synthetic augmentation + Tier 1; Low -> deferred sampling for periodic scans.

Automated label-refresh loop (operational steps):
1) Telemetry ingestion: production traces tagged with slice-id and anomaly flag are forwarded to samplecraft.
2) Prioritization: samplecraft assigns bucket and creates labeling tasks via the labeling vendor API (or internal labeling UI).
3) Human labeling: label-refresher batches tasks in 200–500 units, includes guardrail checks (consistency spot-checks, gold-standard insertion rate 5%).
4) Label quality: labels pass when inter-annotator agreement (IAA) > 0.75 for categorical tasks or correlation > 0.85 for scalar metrics.
5) Recompute slice baselines: new labels are versioned and pushed to the eval corpus.
6) Trigger focused eval: Tier 2 evals run automatically for updated slices; if threshold breach occurs, open a triage runbook.

Gating thresholds and SLOs (example numbers):
- Tier 1 smoke pass: semantic-stability delta <= 0.08 (absolute) vs. baseline; latency p95 < 2x baseline.
- Tier 2 pass: semantic-F1 >= baseline - 0.03 AND hallucination-rate <= baseline + 0.02.
- Tier 3 certification: token-diff ratio <= 1.5% on certified prompt set; KPIs: pass rate >= 95% across certified slices.
- Labeling SLA: 95% of high-priority labeling tasks completed within 72 hours.

Quantization-aware checks:
- Every quantization candidate must run a focused-slice eval that includes: long-context (>4k tokens) prompts, high-KV-cache reuse prompts, and prompts that previously exhibited token-level divergence.
- Capture and compare intermediate logits snapshots where supported; if absolute logit drift above 0.2 occurs on top-10 tokens for >5% of slices flag as high-risk.
- For mixed-precision deployments, ensure ensemble testing (FP16 baseline + quantized variants) on Tier 3 replay before promotion.

Acceptance and promotion flow (condensed):
1) Dev publishes candidate -> Tier 1 smoke executes.
2) If smoke passes, automated scheduling runs Tier 2 focused-slice for quantization and edge-case slices.
3) Passing Tier 2 triggers a controlled Tier 3 replay (gold-standard certification), or for low-risk changes a fast-promote to canary.
4) Canary monitors real traffic for 48–72 hours with telemetry hooks; automated rollback if error_delta > 1.5x or customer-facing regressions detected.

Regression triage playbook (on Tier 2/3 failure):
1) Run triage-assist to collect diffs: token-level diffs, logit-drift summary, top-k answer divergence, and KV-cache hit-rate in replay.
2) Map failure signatures to root-cause classifiers (known classes: quantization, prompt-truncation, tokenization drift, RNG/seed mismatch, model-abi mismatch).
3) If classifier confidence < 0.6, escalate to a human investigation and create a regression incident.
4) Create reproducible fidelity replay job (Tier 3) with telemetry link and annotated hypothesis list.
5) Run controlled experiments: swap quantized kernels, toggle KV-cache modes, and sweep model compilation flags. Record results in a structured triage table.

Triage table (example columns, described):
- experiment-id, hypothesis, knobs-changed, pass/fail, notes, investigator, linked-artifacts.

Operational runbook: step-by-step for on-call (short):
1) Alert receives: eval-alert team->oncall.
2) Run quick-smoke job: evalctl run --suite rapid-smoke --candidate <id> --baseline <id> --timeout 10m.
3) If smoke fails, pin candidate in rollout system and mark canary:do-not-progress.
4) Kick off Tier 2 focused eval with label-refresh trigger.
5) If triage indicates quantization, run quant-sanity script: ./tools/quant-sanity --candidate <id> --slices important-slices.yaml.
6) Document findings in triage incident and route to model-onboarding and runtime-kernel teams.

Example CLI and YAML snippets (textual):
- Quick smoke run:
  evalctl run --suite rapid-smoke --candidate rwm-2026-003 --baseline rwm-stable-2026-01 --out /tmp/smoke.json

- Focused job config (YAML):
  name: focused-slice-job
  candidate: rwm-2026-003
  slices: [enterprise-critical, long-context-8k, kv-heavy]
  labels_required: true
  parallelism: 8
  posthooks: [label-refresh, triage-notify]

Label quality checks (pseudo rules):
- Insert gold items at a 5% rate per batch.
- If a worker fails >2 gold items in the same batch, reject and reassign their tasks.
- Compute batch IAA and only accept batch if IAA >= 0.75.

Appendix A: Common failure signatures and first actions (short catalogue):
- High token-diff concentrated in suffix region -> likely context-truncation or alignment mismatch. Action: run replay with extended context tokens and check tokenization mapping.
- Broad semantic drift across slices but low token-diff -> possible calibration or distributional shift. Action: run focused-slice with alternative temperature and sampler settings.
- Instability only in quantized runtimes -> run quant-sanity sweep and compare logits snapshots.

Appendix B: Example acceptance checklist for promoting quantized variant:
- [ ] Tier 1 smoke: pass
- [ ] Tier 2 focused: semantic-F1 delta <= -0.03
- [ ] Tier 2 hallucination: <= baseline + 0.02
- [ ] Tier 3 fidelity: token-diff <= 1.5% on cert set
- [ ] Labeling IAA >= 0.75 on all new slices
- [ ] Post-canary telemetry stable for 72 hours

Document maintenance:
- Owner: applied-ml-evals. Review cadence: quarterly or after any significant runtime/quantization change.
- Contact: evan.liu@redwood.ai for operational questions, priya.desai@redwood.ai for process questions.
